title: One Band, Three Questions
endLine: A band shows size; antibodies, masses or sequence name the protein.

scenes.tts: Last time, selective loss left a small tube rich in active target. Run a sample on a gel. One clean band appears. Is it one protein, and which protein is it?
scenes.narration: Last time, selective loss left a small tube rich in active target. Run a sample on a gel. One clean band appears. Is it one protein, and which protein is it?
scenes.caption: Last time, selective loss left a small tube rich in active target. Run a sample on a gel. One clean band appears. Is it one protein, and which protein is it?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and COLOUR MAP without a reset: GOLD active target tokens, GREY other-protein tokens, TEAL retained sample and formulas, RED discarded material, BLUE separation controls. No molecular structures anywhere in this film: only labelled disks, vessels, bands, bars, Y-shaped cartoons and bead chains. THE WORLD, carried all film: at LEFT (about 30% of width) the first film's small purified vessel, gold-rich, GOLD tokens orbiting slowly with one or two GREY tokens; at RIGHT (about 65% of width, about 70% of frame height) a tall upright PROVING PANEL that begins as a gel slab with two lanes, left lane 'ladder', right lane 'sample'. A full-opacity 'schematic' label sits at lower right all film. Link-back motion on 'selective loss': a faint RED discard stream leaves the vessel and fades, and a small TEAL tag '30,000 units/mg' flashes on the vessel then fades. On 'Run a sample', a small drop leaves the vessel and falls into the top of the sample lane; it streaks down and settles as ONE sharp GOLD band about two thirds of the way down. On the question, the camera eases toward the band and a large question mark breathes beside it; text across the top: 'One band. Which protein?'
Do not cut away. Title 'One Band, Three Questions' (TITLE_FONT 54) fades in above the proving panel for 2 s while the question text fades out. The GOLD band shimmers; vessel tokens keep orbiting.

scenes.tts: That gel is S D S page. The detergent S D S unfolds each chain and coats it with negative charge. Chains then sort by size alone, the small ones running fastest.
scenes.narration: That gel is SDS-PAGE. The detergent SDS unfolds each chain and coats it with negative charge. Chains then sort by size alone, the small ones running fastest.
scenes.caption: That gel is SDS-PAGE. The detergent SDS unfolds each chain and coats it with negative charge. Chains then sort by size alone, the small ones running fastest.
scenes.visual: Rewind the sample lane: three proteins drawn as different-sized folded GOLD/GREY blobs (a large, a medium, a small one; cartoon blobs, not structures) sit in the well. On 'unfolds', each blob uncoils into a straight bead chain of its own length (long, medium, short). On 'coats it with negative charge', small WHITE minus signs pop along every chain at even spacing, so longer chains carry more of them. A '+' terminal at the bottom of the panel and '-' at the top appear. On 'sort by size alone', the three chains slide down the lane; the short chain runs farthest, the long chain least, and each settles as a band. Only one band (the GOLD one) stays bright; the two demonstration bands fade, leaving the opening's single GOLD band in place. Label at the lane: 'small runs fastest'.

scenes.tts: A ladder of marker proteins, each of known size, runs in the next lane. Read the band against it, and you estimate the chain's size. That is the gel's first answer.
scenes.narration: A ladder of marker proteins, each of known size, runs in the next lane. Read the band against it, and you estimate the chain's size. That is the gel's first answer.
scenes.caption: A ladder of marker proteins, each of known size, runs in the next lane. Read the band against it, and you estimate the chain's size. That is the gel's first answer.
scenes.visual: In the left lane, five TEAL marker bands appear top to bottom, each tagged with a size word only ('large' at top to 'small' at bottom; no kilodalton numbers, schematic). On 'Read the band against it', a horizontal TEAL ruler line slides across from the GOLD band to the ladder and lands between two marker bands; a TEAL tag 'estimated size' appears where it lands. On 'first answer', a small card numbered '1 · size' pins to the top of the panel and stays all film. Vessel tokens keep orbiting at left.

scenes.tts: Its other answer is a first look at purity. One band per kind of chain is needed, but not enough. Two proteins of the same size run together. A contaminant can hide below what the stain detects.
scenes.narration: Its other answer is a first look at purity. One band per kind of chain is needed, but not enough. Two proteins of the same size run together. A contaminant can hide below what the stain detects.
scenes.caption: Its other answer is a first look at purity. One band per kind of chain is needed, but not enough. Two proteins of the same size run together. A contaminant can hide below what the stain detects.
scenes.visual: On 'first look at purity', the GOLD band glows and the lane around it stays clean. On 'needed, but not enough', the camera zooms into the band until it opens like a window: inside, GOLD bead chains lie side by side with one GREY chain of exactly the same length, both at the same height. On 'same size run together', the GREY chain pulses, then the zoom closes and the band looks single again. On 'below what the stain detects', a faint GREY smudge in the lane is drawn at about 10% opacity, barely visible, while a small side-bar meter labelled 'stain limit' shows the smudge's signal sitting just under its dashed TEAL threshold.

scenes.tts: Here is the guiding idea. A band gives a size, not a name. Purity and identity are separate questions. Antibodies, masses and sequence say which protein it is.
scenes.narration: Here is the guiding idea. A band gives a size, not a name. Purity and identity are separate questions. Antibodies, masses and sequence say which protein it is.
scenes.caption: Here is the guiding idea. A band gives a size, not a name. Purity and identity are separate questions. Antibodies, masses and sequence say which protein it is.
scenes.visual: The proving panel briefly lifts to show its full height; the '1 · size' card stays pinned. On 'a size, not a name', a TEAL tag 'size' attaches to the GOLD band and an empty name tag with a blank line dangles beside it. On 'separate questions', two large labels split apart above the panel: 'purity' (TEAL, pointing at the clean lane) and 'identity' (GOLD, pointing at the empty name tag). On the last sentence, two more cards slide in under card 1 and stay all film: '2 · which protein?' and '3 · sequence'. The tokens in the vessel keep orbiting.

scenes.tts: First, antibodies. Copy the gel onto a membrane, band for band. Probe it with an antibody, and only the matching band lights up. A validated antibody supports identity.
scenes.narration: First, antibodies. Copy the gel onto a membrane, band for band. Probe it with an antibody, and only the matching band lights up. A validated antibody supports identity.
scenes.caption: First, antibodies. Copy the gel onto a membrane, band for band. Probe it with an antibody, and only the matching band lights up. A validated antibody supports identity.
scenes.visual: Card '2 · which protein?' glows. The gel panel's surface peels off and transforms into a pale membrane sheet in the same place; label 'membrane'. On 'band for band', a wider sample lane is shown holding several GREY bands from a mixture plus the GOLD band, and every band reappears on the membrane at exactly the same height (ghost lines join each gel band to its copy). On 'antibody', a few PURPLE Y-shaped cartoons (labelled 'antibody', no molecular detail) drift across the membrane; they bump GREY bands and slide off, but clamp onto the GOLD band. On 'lights up', the GOLD band glows bright while all GREY bands fade to 20%. On 'validated antibody', a small tick appears beside the empty name tag, with the tag 'supports identity'. Label: 'western blot'.

scenes.tts: Second, mass. Trypsin cuts the protein into a predictable set of peptides. A laser launches them down a flight tube. Most carry one charge, so heavier ones arrive later.
scenes.narration: Second, mass. Trypsin cuts the protein into a predictable set of peptides. A laser launches them down a flight tube. Most carry one charge, so heavier ones arrive later.
scenes.caption: Second, mass. Trypsin cuts the protein into a predictable set of peptides. A laser launches them down a flight tube. Most carry one charge, so heavier ones arrive later.
scenes.visual: The membrane rotates a quarter turn and transforms into a long horizontal FLIGHT TUBE spanning the panel, a 'laser' flash point at left, a 'detector' plate at right. The GOLD band lifts out as a single GOLD bead chain. On 'Trypsin cuts', small BLUE scissors snip it at fixed points into six GOLD segments of different lengths, labelled 'peptides'. On 'A laser launches', a flash fires and all six segments leave together from the left. On 'heavier ones arrive later', they spread out by length as they fly: the shortest reaches the detector first, the longest last. Label under the tube: 'MALDI-TOF'. The vessel keeps orbiting at far left.

scenes.tts: Arrival times give each peptide's mass, to a fraction of a dalton. But you never read a single amino acid. Can a list of masses name the protein?
scenes.narration: Arrival times give each peptide's mass, to a fraction of a dalton. But you never read a single amino acid. Can a list of masses name the protein?
scenes.caption: Arrival times give each peptide's mass, to a fraction of a dalton. But you never read a single amino acid. Can a list of masses name the protein?
scenes.visual: As each segment hits the detector, a GOLD vertical stick rises on a readout strip beneath the tube; six sticks stand at six positions, axis 'mass' with no numbers (schematic). The sticks compress into a short GOLD list of six ticks labelled 'mass list'. On 'never read a single amino acid', the six GOLD segments show no internal letters; a small crossed-out letter icon appears. On the question, the empty name tag swings beside the mass list and a large breathing question mark appears. Question card (TEXT 38): 'Can masses name it?'

Deliberate thinking pause. Hold 'Can masses name it?', the GOLD mass list and the empty name tag. Near silence. The question mark breathes from scale 1.0 to 1.06 and back; the vessel's GOLD tokens orbit slowly at left. No other change.

scenes.tts: For a known protein, yes. A computer predicts the trypsin digest of every protein in a database. Few proteins give the same set of masses. The list works like a fingerprint.
scenes.narration: For a known protein, yes. A computer predicts the trypsin digest of every protein in a database. Few proteins give the same set of masses. The list works like a fingerprint.
scenes.caption: For a known protein, yes. A computer predicts the trypsin digest of every protein in a database. Few proteins give the same set of masses. The list works like a fingerprint.
scenes.visual: The question card flips to 'yes, if known'. A tall stack of GREY database cards appears at right, each carrying its own row of six GREY ticks at different positions (schematic). On 'predicts', the stack fans out. On 'Few proteins give the same set', the GOLD mass list slides along the stack; at each card the ticks mismatch and the card dims, until one card's ticks line up with all six GOLD ticks and it turns GOLD. On 'fingerprint', the matching ticks merge into a fingerprint-like whorl of six arcs, and a GOLD name appears on the dangling name tag: 'match found'. The tick for card '2 · which protein?' turns solid.

scenes.tts: Third, sequence. Edman degradation clips the first residue off the chain, names it, and repeats. Each cycle is only about ninety-eight percent efficient. So long proteins are cut into overlapping peptides and read in pieces.
scenes.narration: Third, sequence. Edman degradation clips the first residue off the chain, names it, and repeats. Each cycle is only about 98% efficient. So long proteins are cut into overlapping peptides and read in pieces.
scenes.caption: Third, sequence. Edman degradation clips the first residue off the chain, names it, and repeats. Each cycle is only about 98% efficient. So long proteins are cut into overlapping peptides and read in pieces.
scenes.visual: Card '3 · sequence' glows. The flight tube shortens back into the upright panel and one long GOLD bead chain stands in it, start of the chain at top labelled 'start (N-terminus)'. On 'clips the first residue', the top bead pops off, flies to a small reader box and receives a letter tag; the next bead pops off and repeats, a steady rhythm. On 'ninety-eight percent', a few chains beside it fall slightly out of step, so their beads pop a beat late and the reader box begins to blur (no fraction shown). On 'cut into overlapping peptides', two copies of the long chain are cut at different sites into shorter GOLD pieces whose ends overlap, laid out like shingles, each read cleanly.

scenes.tts: The modern answer is tandem mass spectrometry. One peptide breaks into a ladder of pieces, each one residue shorter. Each gap between peaks matches one amino acid. Leucine and isoleucine weigh the same, so blind spots remain.
scenes.narration: The modern answer is tandem mass spectrometry. One peptide breaks into a ladder of pieces, each one residue shorter. Each gap between peaks matches one amino acid. Leucine and isoleucine weigh the same, so blind spots remain.
scenes.caption: The modern answer is tandem mass spectrometry. One peptide breaks into a ladder of pieces, each one residue shorter. Each gap between peaks matches one amino acid. Leucine and isoleucine weigh the same, so blind spots remain.
scenes.visual: The panel becomes the flight tube again, now labelled 'tandem MS'. One GOLD peptide enters and breaks into a staircase of pieces, each exactly one bead shorter than the last. On 'gap between peaks', the pieces become GOLD sticks on the readout strip; brackets span each gap between neighbouring sticks, and each bracket receives a one-letter tag, so a short row of letters builds left to right. On 'Leucine and isoleucine', two gaps of identical width glow and their tag shows 'L or I' with a question mark; label 'same mass'.

scenes.tts: Frederick Sanger spent twelve years reading the fifty-one amino acids of insulin by hand. Today, mass spectrometry can identify a protein from its peptides in a single run.
scenes.narration: Frederick Sanger spent 12 years reading the 51 amino acids of insulin by hand. Today, mass spectrometry can identify a protein from its peptides in a single run.
scenes.caption: Frederick Sanger spent 12 years reading the 51 amino acids of insulin by hand. Today, mass spectrometry can identify a protein from its peptides in a single run.
scenes.visual: Left half of the panel: two linked chains of 21 and 30 small GOLD beads (51 in all), filled in one at a time while a counter labelled 'years' ticks from 0 to 12; tag 'Sanger, insulin'. Right half: one tandem-MS readout strip that sweeps once and fills with sticks in a few seconds, tag 'one run'. Both halves keep moving: the bead chain shimmers bead by bead; the readout's sweep line repeats. No portrait.

scenes.tts: So one clean band opens the question of identity. It does not close it. Size comes from the gel; the name comes from antibodies, masses or sequence.
scenes.narration: So one clean band opens the question of identity. It does not close it. Size comes from the gel; the name comes from antibodies, masses or sequence.
scenes.caption: So one clean band opens the question of identity. It does not close it. Size comes from the gel; the name comes from antibodies, masses or sequence.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening picture: the gold-rich vessel at left, the upright gel panel with ladder and the single GOLD band. The three cards '1 · size', '2 · which protein?', '3 · sequence' stand beside the panel. On 'opens the question', the band briefly opens its window again to show the hidden same-size GREY chain, then closes. On 'Size comes from the gel', card 1 links by a TEAL line to the ladder. On 'antibodies, masses or sequence', small icons (PURPLE Y, GOLD tick list, GOLD letter row) slide onto card 2 and card 3 and all three link to the band's name tag, which now reads 'identity'. Tokens keep orbiting.

End card over the living world at 25% opacity: the vessel's GOLD tokens orbit slowly and the GOLD band shimmers. LINE (TITLE_FONT 40): 'A band shows size; antibodies, masses or sequence name the protein.'
